candidates.title: He Grew Gap To $14B — Then Got Fired
candidates.description: We sit down with Mickey Drexler — the retail legend who built the modern American wardrobe. Over an 18-year run he grew Gap from $400 million to $14 billion in sales, founded Old Navy and turned it into the fastest brand ever to hit $1 billion, personally bought the Madewell name for $125,000, and later ran J.Crew. Steve Jobs put him on Apple's board, where he helped design the Apple Store — and then called him the night before Gap fired him with one day's notice. Today he's chairman of Alex Mill, the brand founded by his son. Netflix's Newest Blockbuster Isn't Something You Watch
candidates.description: Netflix is turning your phone into a video game controller. On June 30 it launches Unhinged, an interactive horror game starring Zoe Kravitz and Sadie Sink, where you scan a QR code and your real phone becomes the flashlight your character uses to survive the dark. When a killer calls from inside the game, your actual phone rings. Netflix has quietly had games since 2021 with almost nothing to show for it, so why is it now spending Hollywood money to build a console-free game for people who don't even play games? Google's $75M A24 Deal Could Reshape Every Movie
candidates.description: Google just took a $75 million equity stake in A24 — its first-ever investment in a film studio — and tied it to a multi-year AI research partnership with DeepMind. While most of Hollywood is busy suing AI companies for copyright infringement, the anti-blockbuster studio behind Everything Everywhere All at Once is doing the exact opposite. The DeepMind tools are aimed at reshoots, editing, and VFX rather than generating films outright. We get into why Google is double-dipping on the future of Hollywood — it already owns YouTube — and whether this deal is a genuine creative breakthrough or something we're calling "taste-washing." Then, Grillo's Pickles added 100,000 followers in a single week
